haiku-low.q1: Only a short-lived challenge. No session is created until the second factor passes.
haiku-low.q2: Only after the user enters a valid code from the new app, which activates it. Sign-in ignores pending secrets until then.
haiku-low.q3: The unused code is claimed and sign-in creates a session. The email is queued, not awaited, and sign-in still succeeds if queuing fails.
haiku-low.q4: A 5th wrong entry, or 5 minutes passing, deletes the challenge. The user goes back to the password step.
haiku-low.q5: On confirming setup, all other sessions are deleted and the current sid is kept. Recovery codes are also replaced.
haiku-low.q6: No. A step is accepted once, and steps at or below last_used_step are refused. Drift tolerated: the current step plus one step either side, about 30 seconds.
haiku-low.q7: In one transaction: secret becomes active, last_used_step is set, 10 new recovery codes issued, other sessions deleted. Partial-failure behaviour is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q8: In a server-side login_challenges row, with the raw token in a separate short-lived challenge cookie, not sid. Removed on success, 5th wrong entry, or expiry.
haiku-low.q9: totp_factors row holds sealed active and pending secrets plus last_used_step. recovery_codes holds sha256 hashes and used_at. 2FA on means an active secret is set.
haiku-low.q10: Old active secret keeps protecting sign-in; pending is ignored. Abandonment is NOT STATED; the doc says only that starting again overwrites pending.
haiku-low.q11: NOT STATED how the code type is told apart. Yes, wrong recovery codes count: any entry not accepted adds 1 to wrong_attempts.
haiku-low.q12: Not decided. No transition is drawn; product must decide whether support may reset 2FA and how identity is checked.

sonnet.q1: Only a short-lived challenge (a login_challenges row plus challenge cookie). No session, no sid; it gives access to nothing.
sonnet.q2: Only once confirmed: the new secret is pending and ignored by sign-in until the user enters a valid code from it; then it becomes active. Sign-in checks only active_secret_sealed.
sonnet.q3: The recovery code is claimed (marked used via UPDATE ... WHERE used_at IS NULL), a normal sid session is created, and a 'recovery_code_used' email with the remaining count is queued after commit. Sign-in does not depend on the email: it is not awaited, failed sends are retried in the background, and a queuing failure does not fail sign-in.
sonnet.q4: The 5th wrong entry, or more than 5 minutes since creation (checked on any request). The challenge row is deleted and the user starts again from the password check.
sonnet.q5: All of the user's other sessions are deleted (current sid kept), in the same transaction as activation, along with issuing 10 new recovery codes.
sonnet.q6: No. A step at or below last_used_step is refused (replay protection, via a conditional update), so the same code cannot be reused; it also rejects older never-used steps. Tolerance is the current 30-second step plus one step before and one after.
sonnet.q7: In one transaction: the pending secret becomes active (setup: secret becomes active; replacement: swap), last_used_step is set to the matching step, recovery codes are replaced with 10 new ones, and other sessions are deleted (current sid kept). A wrong or reused code changes nothing (no codes issued, no sessions deleted). What happens if the transaction fails partway is NOT STATED beyond its being one transaction.
sonnet.q8: In a server-side login_challenges row (token_hash PK = sha256 of the cookie value, user_id, expires_at = creation + 5 minutes, wrong_attempts). The browser holds the raw token in its own short-lived challenge cookie (not sid). The row is deleted on success, on the 5th wrong entry, and on expiry.
sonnet.q9: Secret and enrolment status: totp_factors (one row per user): active_secret_sealed and pending_secret_sealed, both sealed with AES-GCM using a KMS app key. Replay state: last_used_step in totp_factors. Recovery codes: recovery_codes table (user_id, sha256 code_hash, used_at). 2FA on is determined by column state: active set and pending NULL = On (active and pending both set = ReplacementPending, which is also on); no row = Off; pending only = SetupPending (not on).
sonnet.q10: The old active secret stays active and keeps working for sign-in; the new secret is only pending and ignored at sign-in. Abandoning: NOT STATED explicitly (the doc says the old secret keeps working and starting again presumably overwrites pending, but it gives no cleanup or expiry for an abandoned replacement).
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED how the server distinguishes the two input types. The doc only says an entry that matches neither a valid TOTP nor an unused recovery code is a wrong entry. Yes, a wrong recovery code is a wrong entry and adds 1 to wrong_attempts (as does a reused recovery code with no row claimed).
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED / undecided. The doc lists it as an open question: no transition is drawn; product must decide whether support can reset 2FA and how identity would be verified.
